connection.title: Connection Settings
connection.description: Enter connection endpoints as hostname:port. The application domain is the domain registered on developer.tesla.com — required for partner account registration and virtual key pairing.

data_description.domain: Your app's root domain from developer.tesla.com allowed_origins. Used for partner account registration and the virtual key pairing URL.
data_description.mqtt_topic_base: The topic_base configured in your fleet-telemetry server's config (default: tesla).
data_description.mqtt_username: Leave empty if your broker allows anonymous connections.
data_description.mqtt_tls: Connect with TLS; the broker certificate must be trusted by the system CA store.
data_description.proxy_verify_ssl: Enable only if the proxy uses a publicly trusted certificate. Leave off for the usual self-signed proxy certificate.
data_description.telemetry_mode: Realtime ≈1 s, Normal ≈10 s, Low ≈30 s per field. Locks, doors and other binary states always stream at 1 s. Use the quietest mode that fits.

init.title: Disable Unknown Field Entity
init.description:
The telemetry field `{field}` for vehicle **{vin}** is not recognized by Tesla. Click **Submit** to acknowledge and disable the related entity.

You can manually re-enable it in Settings → Devices & Services if needed.

init.title: Telemetry Server Certificate Expired — {vin}
init.description:
The TLS certificate of your telemetry server (`{target}`) has **expired**, so the vehicle cannot connect and **no telemetry is received**.

1. Renew the certificate on the telemetry server host.
2. Replace `fullchain.pem` / `privkey.pem` and restart the fleet-telemetry container.

When you have done that, press **Submit** to reload the integration. It re-reads the server's certificate chain and pushes the configuration to the vehicle again.

abort.entry_not_found: Could not find the Tesla Fleet Telemetry entry for this vehicle.
abort.reloaded: **Integration reloaded.** It reconnected and pushed the configuration again. The server's certificate chain is unchanged. If the problem persists the issue will reappear here on its own.
abort.reloaded_ca_changed: **Integration reloaded.** The server's certificate chain changed, so the new CA was stored and pushed to the vehicle. A sleeping vehicle only applies it when it wakes, which can take a few minutes. If the problem persists the issue will reappear here on its own.

init.title: Telemetry Server Certificate Invalid — {vin}
init.description:
The vehicle rejected the TLS certificate of `{target}` (untrusted, wrong hostname or incomplete chain), so **no telemetry is received**.

Use a publicly trusted certificate with the full chain whose name matches the telemetry server hostname, then restart the fleet-telemetry container.

When you have done that, press **Submit** to reload the integration. It re-reads the server's certificate chain and pushes the configuration to the vehicle again.

init.title: Telemetry Server Unreachable — {vin}
init.description:
The vehicle cannot reach `{target}` (connection refused, timeout or DNS failure), so **no telemetry is received**.

Check that the fleet-telemetry container is running, DNS points to your public IP and the port is forwarded/open.

When you have done that, press **Submit** to reload the integration. It re-reads the server's certificate chain and pushes the configuration to the vehicle again.

init.description:
Tesla reports that this vehicle's hardware does not support Fleet Telemetry. Streaming cannot work for **{vin}**; remove the integration entry for it.

When you have done that, press **Submit** to reload the integration. It re-reads the server's certificate chain and pushes the configuration to the vehicle again.
